subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A test is administered only once. The teacher then divides the test into odd-numbered and even-numbered items, scores each half separately, and correlates the two sets of scores to estimate reliability. This method is called:
explanation: Split-half reliability estimates internal consistency from a single administration by comparing scores on two halves of the same test — unlike test-retest (two administrations of the same test over time) or parallel-forms (two different but equivalent test versions).

subject: Educational Psychology
stem: Two different but equivalent versions of the same test (matched in content, difficulty, and length) are administered to the same group, and the scores on both versions are correlated to check consistency. This method of estimating reliability is called:
explanation: Parallel-forms reliability uses two equivalent test versions on the same group to check consistency, avoiding the memory/practice effects that can inflate test-retest correlations.

stem: Over the year, a student compiles a purposeful collection of their best written work, art projects, and reflective notes, showing growth and effort over time, which the teacher reviews periodically instead of relying only on term-end exams. This assessment tool is called a:
explanation: A portfolio is a purposeful, ongoing collection of a student's work samples that documents growth, effort, and achievement over time — a key tool of continuous and comprehensive evaluation (CCE).

section: Educational Psychology · Ch13 — Assessment: Reliability & Tools (Complete)
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: Before grading student essays, a teacher prepares a scoring guide that clearly describes what performance looks like at each level (e.g., 'excellent', 'good', 'needs improvement') for criteria like organisation, argument, and grammar, ensuring consistent and transparent grading. This scoring guide is called a:
explanation: A rubric is a scoring guide listing explicit criteria and performance-level descriptors, used to make subjective assessment (like essay grading) more consistent, objective, and transparent to students.

stem: A good educational test is expected to give the same score regardless of who scores it (not depending on the examiner's personal judgement or mood). This essential characteristic of a good test is known as:
explanation: Objectivity means scoring is free from the examiner's personal bias or judgement — distinct from reliability (consistency across repeated administration) and validity (measures what it claims to measure). Objectivity, reliability, validity, and usability together form the four key characteristics of a good test.
